title: Attribute post-rotation authentication failures to a disabled secret version or a stale reference
telemetry: Supplied Cloud Logging cloud_run_revision request and application records, a secret-owner Secret Manager version-metadata and access-outcome summary, and custodian-gateway owner records, compiled into one export released through a protected fixture CLI. No live Cloud Logging, Secret Manager or gateway access; no secret payload, token or key material.
owner: Harper, Custody on-call, owns the investigation; Ellis, the secret owner, owns custodian-gateway-credential versions and the rotation; the release owner decides any revision or secret-reference change; Marlowe, the custodian-gateway integration owner, owns which credentials the gateway accepts. ITO coordinates the existing TLC.
task: Harper needs a technical update on custody-sync's custodian-gateway authentication failures, which began after the 13:30 UTC credential rotation. Use the available bounded read interface to inspect the service, secret-reference and log records, then report the supported failing step, the evidence and unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner for the existing TLC. Work from metadata and sanitized errors only: no secret payload, token or key material may be requested or read, and no secret, IAM, revision, traffic or downstream change is authorized.

sources.claim: A secret mounted as a volume is fetched from Secret Manager when the file is read, which suits rotation; secret environment variables are resolved at instance startup, so Google recommends pinning them rather than using latest. Deployment checks that the service identity can access the secrets, volume startup does not, and reads of a mounted volume fail if the secret becomes inaccessible at runtime. The service identity needs roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor. The page does not describe disabled versions or the error an application sees, so the fixture's read_failed record is authored.

A secret version is ENABLED, DISABLED or DESTROYED; a disabled version cannot be accessed, and re-enabling it restores access. No error code for accessing a disabled version is documented, so the fixture's failed-precondition wording is a paraphrase and is not graded.
DISABLED: the version may not be accessed, but the secret data is still available and can be placed back into ENABLED. DESTROYED: the data is no longer stored and the version cannot leave that state.

Accessing a version returns the secret data and requires secretmanager.versions.access; versions/latest is an alias for the most recently created version. The case reads metadata only and never calls access.

roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor allows accessing the payload of secrets through secretmanager.versions.access; Viewer covers metadata, and Editor and Viewer do not include payload access, so metadata review needs no payload-reading grant.

Cloud Run service logs use resource type cloud_run_revision with service_name, revision_name, location and project_id labels, and container stdout/stderr is associated with that resource. The Secret Manager access-outcome summary and the gateway records are authored owner observations, not native Cloud Run log entries.

a.conclusion: The revision's secret volume pins custodian-gateway-credential version 7, which the CHG-6121 rotation automation disabled at 14:00:07 UTC. Every later runtime read of that version fails, the application logs a credential-load failure before each CUSTODIAN_AUTH_FAILED, and it sends no gateway authentication request. The gateway still accepts the version-7 credential and saw no attempt, so a downstream rejection of a stale credential is not supported. The runtime holds secretAccessor, so this is a version-state failure, not a permission gap. Why a referenced version was disabled is not established.
next_checks: Ellis confirms the 14:00:07 disable of version 7 by the CHG-6121 automation and lists every consumer that still references version 7.

Ellis and the release owner decide through change approval between re-enabling version 7 (a disable retains its data, and Marlowe accepts cg-cred-2026-07 until 2026-10-20) and a reviewed revision that references version 8 after Marlowe confirms cg-cred-2026-10 is accepted for custody-sync; this investigation applies neither.
Harper reports recovery on the existing TLC only from correlated metadata: a successful version read, a custodian-gateway session and POST /positions/sync 200s after an owner-approved change.
unsupported: Diagnose a stale reference or say custodian-gateway rejects the version-7 credential; the gateway still accepts it and received no attempts.
Redeploy to version 8 or latest, roll back, or re-enable version 7 as an applied or approved fix without the secret and release owners' decision.
Grant broader Secret Manager or project IAM roles; the runtime already holds roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor and the failure is the version's state.
Read, print or compare secret payloads, or request tokens or key material; value comparison belongs to the secret owner.
Destroy version 7 or treat DISABLED as DESTROYED; a destroyed version cannot be restored.
Declare recovery without a correlated successful read, gateway session and request completion.
unknowns: Why the rotation automation disabled a version that revision custody-sync-00027-wab still references.
Service state after the 14:20 owner-record and 14:24 application-log coverage cutoffs.

b.conclusion: Version 7 is ENABLED and every runtime read of it succeeds, so Secret Manager access is not the failing step. custodian-gateway retired cg-cred-2026-07, the version-7 credential, at 14:00:00 UTC under CHG-6121 and now accepts only cg-cred-2026-10 (version 8); it rejected all 57 custody-sync attempts presenting the retired identifier. Revision custody-sync-00027-wab's volume still pins version 7, so the application is using a stale secret reference after the rotation. Why the reference was not moved is not established.
next_checks: Release owner, with the application owner, prepares a reviewed revision whose secret reference selects version 8, pinned or deliberately latest on the volume, for change approval; this investigation applies nothing.

Marlowe confirms cg-cred-2026-10 is accepted for custody-sync's client before any cutover; Ellis confirms version 8 is the intended current version and lists other consumers still pinning version 7 before any later disable.
Harper reports recovery on the existing TLC only from correlated metadata: a successful version-8 read, an accepted gateway session and POST /positions/sync 200s after an owner-approved change.
unsupported: Diagnose a disabled or inaccessible version, or re-enable a version; version 7 is enabled and every read succeeds.
Grant secretAccessor or broader IAM roles; the runtime already holds the accessor role and reads succeed.
Read, print or compare secret payloads to prove staleness, or request tokens or key material; the key identifiers and owner records suffice, and value comparison belongs to the secret owner.
Redeploy or roll back as an applied fix without release-owner approval, or ask the gateway to re-accept the retired credential without Marlowe's decision.
Disable or destroy version 7 now; other consumers may still pin it.
Present a secret environment variable referencing latest as rotation-safe; environment variables resolve at instance startup and go stale on running instances.
Declare recovery without a correlated successful session and request completion.
unknowns: Why CHG-6121 did not move custody-sync's reference to version 8.
Service state after the 14:20 owner-record and 14:24 application-log coverage cutoffs.
